suggestions.rationale: Obstructive sleep apnea is frequently identified in cohorts with interstitial lung disease, but the available meta-analysis is prevalence evidence and does not establish that ILD causes or aggravates OSA in an individual. A systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 studies involving 569 patients with ILD found OSA in 61% and described the result as preliminary evidence of high OSA prevalence in ILD. This mapping therefore remains association-focused and requires sleep-study confirmation, ILD phenotype/severity, chronology, body-habitus and upper-airway risk factors, medication context, and specialist assessment before any individual secondary theory is advanced.
evidenceGaps: Polysomnography or validated sleep-study documentation confirming OSA and severity
Pulmonology documentation establishing the ILD subtype, severity, physiology, and chronology
OSA chronology relative to ILD onset/progression
BMI/weight trajectory, craniofacial/upper-airway factors, age, smoking, sedating medication, and other OSA risk factors
Pulmonary/sleep specialist assessment distinguishing coexistence from individual causation or aggravation

sourceReferences.citation: Cheng Y, Wang Y, Dai L. The prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea in interstitial lung disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Sleep Breath. 2021;25(3):1219-1228. PMID 33403599
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review/meta-analysis of 10 studies and 569 ILD patients found OSA in 61% and characterized the evidence as preliminary evidence of high OSA prevalence in ILD. Supports association-focused research, not individual causal attribution.
